body:
## Problem

Two repo-wide filesystem walkers decide what to skip from a hardcoded directory-name set that includes `.worktrees`. This repository keeps its worktrees at `.claude/worktrees/` (see `.git/info/exclude:11`), so both walkers descend into stale, untracked worktree checkouts and treat another branch's files as this checkout's content.

### Site 1 — the red test suite

`packages/spec-lint/test/readme-exit-codes.test.mjs:69` scans every `.md`/`.mdx` in the repo for docs still claiming spec-lint exits 0 on a zero-criteria spec. It descends into `.claude/worktrees/` and reports 8 offenders from dead branches. `node scripts/run-tests.mjs` exits 1 (53/54 segments). Tracked docs are clean: `git ls-files '*.md' '*.mdx' | xargs grep -nEi 'no criteria found|nothing to check'` finds no stale claim, so the shipped product is correct and CI is green — the test simply is not hermetic.

### Site 2 — shipped code in @adlc/tickets

`packages/tickets/lib/manifest-rails.mjs:25` has the identical blind spot. `discoverManifests()` returns 146 paths in this checkout, of which **95 come from `.claude/worktrees/`**. `packages/tickets/lib/service.mjs:85` feeds that list to `#assertNoManifestRails`, which throws `RAIL_COVERS_MANIFEST` and refuses to create the ticket.

Measured effect: a rail of `.claude/**` is rejected on a machine that has worktrees and accepted on a clean checkout of the same commit. The error text ("Rail the source subtree instead") does not apply, because the manifest it matched is not one any release rewrites. The function's own doc comment claims "Testing a rail against real paths is exact" — that claim is false while phantom paths are in the list.

## Fix

Skip any directory that is itself a git checkout, instead of guessing directory names. A linked worktree has a `.git` FILE; a submodule or nested clone has a `.git` directory. Either way the subtree is not this checkout's content. Keep the existing `skipDirs` set as a fast path.

This is chosen over adding `.claude` to the lists because the name is not the invariant: the next operator's worktrees land in `.wt/`, `worktrees/`, or a tool-specific directory, and the class reopens. It is chosen over `git ls-files` because `discoverManifests` documents working in a non-git tree and must keep doing so.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `discoverManifests()` returns no path under a nested git checkout.
   Verify: `node --test packages/tickets/test/manifest-rails.test.mjs` — a new case builds a temp root containing a nested directory with a `.git` file plus a `package.json`, and asserts the manifest is absent from the result.
2. A rail's verdict does not depend on whether a nested checkout is present.
   Verify: the same test asserts `coversManifest('.claude/**', discoverManifests(root))` is identical with and without the nested checkout in place.
3. The spec-lint doc scan ignores nested checkouts.
   Verify: `node --test packages/spec-lint/test/readme-exit-codes.test.mjs` exits 0 in a checkout that has `.claude/worktrees/` populated.
4. The full suite is green.
   Verify: `env -u ADLC_TICKET node scripts/run-tests.mjs` exits 0 and prints 54/54 segments passed.
5. No behaviour change for trees without nested checkouts.
   Verify: `node --test packages/tickets/test/manifest-rails.test.mjs packages/spec-lint/test/` — all pre-existing cases pass unmodified.

## Out of scope

`scripts/release.mjs:289` (`hostDiscoveryNearMisses`) reads only one level deep and never reaches a worktree's interior; `scripts/release-audit-collect.mjs:39` was measured returning the correct 38 publish targets. Neither is changed here.
title: Walkers must skip nested git checkouts, not a hardcoded worktree directory name
